reason: Verified by driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-editing. The defect is real and the gate cannot see it. At 1440 and 1280 the .b-stepRead box is 326px and the round-2 string 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days' measures 336px natural in Geist Mono 15px/0.04em, so it wraps and widows 'days' alone on line two (range-measured: line 1 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 ', line 2 'days'). Two presses of -7 shorten it to 'Saturday 25 July 2026 · in 9 days', the box collapses 45px→23px and everything below moves 22px: .b-seg y 814→792, Done and Delete this moment y 862→840; +7 puts them back. min-height is absent on .b-stepRead (b.css:465-472) so nothing reserves the second line. The finding understates two things rather than overstating: the overflow is 10px, not ~2px, and at 390 it is worse than described — the sheet is bottom-anchored, so the four stepper buttons themselves move 22px (y 694→716), i.e. the button under the cursor does move at phone width. interaction-check.mjs only samples .b-step boxes at 1440, where they are genuinely still, so this is not a restatement of a proven assertion. Only 768 is stable, because the sheet goes full width. The fix as written is half wrong: taking the readout off mono would break the register. The same date is printed twice on this screen — .b-date in the row and .b-stepRead in the editor — and the count (.b-away), the stepper faces (.b-step) and the date input (.b-input[data-mono]) are all mono. Making the one string sans would set a sans date beside a mono date thirteen pixels apart and trade a layout defect for a typographic inconsistency, so the family stays. The second half of the fix is the whole fix.
sharpenedFix: Keep font-family: var(--mono) and letter-spacing: var(--track-data) on .b-stepRead — the family is not the bug, the unreserved box is. In b.css add min-height: 45px (two lines at 15px/1.5) to .b-stepRead. Verified in-page: with that one declaration the .b-seg (814), Done (862) and the steppers (660) hold identical positions across the long and short strings at 1440, and at 390 the steppers hold at 694 instead of dropping to 716. Do not rely on text-wrap: balance to fix the widow — tested, it breaks the date itself ('Saturday 8 August' / '2026 · in 23 days'), which is a worse break than the widow. If the widow is to go, force the break at the '·' by rendering the readout as two whole-unit spans (date, then 'in N days') rather than one text node, and update the same two spans in the readout branch of the update path in render-b.js (~line 333) — note that path currently does read.textContent = ..., which would destroy any child spans, and interaction-check.mjs asserts the readout text contains a plain-space 'in N days', so no non-breaking space.
